<description>
Currently the GetTransaction return value is a nullable transaction
pointer, where nullptr represents two different outcomes: I/O error and
missing tx.

Reporting a confirmed transaction as missing is wrong, so properly
return an error instead.
</description>

[2026-10-16] r:5546709537 review COMMENTED by musaHaruna (contributor):
While testing this, I think I might have found another case where `FindTx()` returns `nullopt` instead of throwing.

I first confirmed that a transaction could be retrieved, then deliberately damaged part of the test’s temporary transaction-index database. LevelDB detected the corruption, but `FindTx()` still returned `nullopt` without throwing. Restoring the original data made the lookup work again.

It looks like the candidate scan checks whether the iterator has a valid entry, but does not check whether a database error occurred. That means a failed lookup can be treated as an ordinary missing transaction.

Could we add this to the public methods of `CDBIterator` in `dbwrapper.h`?
```cpp
/** Throw dbwrapper_error if the iterator encountered a database error. */
void CheckStatus() const;
```
Then implement it in `dbwrapper.cpp`, using the existing error handler to throw when LevelDB reports an error:

```cpp
void CDBIterator::CheckStatus() const
{
    HandleError(m_impl_iter->iter->status());
}
```
Finally, call it immediately after the candidate-collection loop in `FindTx()`, before the iterator goes out of scope:

```cpp
candidates.emplace_back(
            tx_position,
            candidate_block_hash,
            key.pos.block_seq,
            m_chainstate->m_chain.Contains(*block_index));
    }

    it->CheckStatus();
}
```
This would let an ordinary missing transaction still return `nullopt`, while reporting a database error instead of silently treating it as missing.
